standard.title: Reflect on how identity is shaped by language and culture
standard.description: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), attitudes, beliefs and values
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity including through contact language influences and modern change (AC9LS6U04). They have not yet analysed how formality signals social relationships, explored the global distribution of the target language, or examined co-official language contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — including language variation as social signal, co-official language identity, and the global distribution of the target language.

nodes.label: Language variation as identity and social signal
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how language variation in the target language — regional vocabulary, formality levels, language change reflecting social values — signals identity and social relationships.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how at least two language variation features signal identity or social relationship — not only describe that they differ.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise how cultural and religious traditions are encoded in naming conventions and common expressions; identify language changes reflecting shifting social values; compare body language, personal space and silence across cultural contexts; identify formality levels and what they reveal about social relationships; compare communicative conventions across cultural contexts.
wider: Analyse a language reform or social language debate in the target language community — explain what each position reflects about cultural values and social change
Compare how different address forms are used across at least three target language communities — explain the social and relational meanings each carries in each context
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding language variation as a social and identity signal — not merely regional difference — is the conceptual prerequisite for the evaluative identity work at subsequent bands. Students who treat variation as arbitrary cannot engage with critical analysis of how language encodes values and power.

response_modes.reason: Explaining language variation as identity signal requires the analytical move from observation to interpretation. Structured analysis tasks — examining the same feature across different social contexts — scaffold this interpretive move.

success_criteria: Explains how at least two language variation features signal identity or social relationship — not only describes that they differ
Identifies at least one language change that reflects changing social values and explains the connection

nodes.label: Global distribution, co-official languages and First Nations connections
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the global distribution of the target language — including communities where it coexists with other languages — and reflect on co-official language identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain at least two aspects of the target language's global distribution; explain why co-official or regional languages are significant for identity in at least one target language community.
nodes.typical_width: Understand the target language in global contexts; explore how target language culture has influenced other languages and cultures; examine co-official and regional language situations and their importance for identity; compare regional vocabulary variation across target language communities; examine First Nations Australian language connections to Country and compare with language variation across target language communities.
wider: Research the co-official language situation in one target language community — explain what it means for speakers' identity and compare with the situation of First Nations languages in Australia
Examine a community where the target language exists alongside other languages — explain the identity stakes for each language community involved

response_modes.reason: Global target language awareness and co-official language understanding develops through encountering the genuine diversity of target language communities across varied geopolitical and cultural contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing co-official language situations in target language communities with the situation of First Nations languages in Australia connects language learning to significant questions of cultural survival, sovereignty and identity — one of the richest intercultural inquiry opportunities in the sequence.
success_criteria: Explains at least two aspects of the target language's global distribution
Explains why co-official or regional languages are significant for identity in at least one target language community
